exposure: first trimester cytological cervical cancer screening results (negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy (NILM) vs. abnormal cytology)
cohort: The study included 18 patients diagnosed with invasive cervical cancer during pregnancy or within 1 year after delivery from 2010 to 2018 at Hokkaido University Hospital.
finding: Cytological examinations of pregnant women may result in presumed false-negative or underestimation, delaying additional examinations to find invasive cervical cancer.
